semantic_fragments.content: The risk management process will be conducted in accordance with standard ISO 14971:2019, EN ISO 14971:2019 and EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021. The risk management plan covers the whole life-cycle of the medical device across the following phases: Initial development, Prototype phase (Design verification), Design validation, Design change, and Production and post-production activities.

Initial development phase activities: 1. Document intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse of the medical device; 2. Identify characteristics related to safety; 3. Identify hazards and hazardous situations; 4. Estimate the risk(s) of each hazardous situation; 5. Risk evaluation; 6. Draft the risk control measures plan. Responsibilities: Project manager shall organize activities; members of risk management shall review job content. Output: Report of risk assessment.

Prototype phase (Design verification) activities: 1. Verify the implementation and effectiveness of risk control measures plan; 2. Assess the residual risk; 3. Make benefit-risk analysis; 4. Evaluate whether there are any risks arising from risk control measures; 5. Review completeness of risk control. Output: Report of verification of risk control measure and residual risk evaluation.
Design validation phase activities: 1. Overall residual risk evaluation; 2. Form the risk management report. Output: Report of risk management.

Design change phase activities: 1. Identify hazards and hazardous situations related to design change; 2. Evaluate risk(s) in hazardous situations resulting from design change; 3. Assess risk(s) in design change; 4. Draft the plan of risk control measures for design change; 5. Verify the implementation of plan on risk control measures after design change; 6. Assess residual risk, benefit-risk analysis and any new risks after design change; 7. Overall residual risk evaluation after design change. Outputs: Record of risk evaluation (when there is no new risk); Report of verification of risk control measure and residual risk evaluation in design change; Report of Risk Management in design change.

Production and post-production activities: 1. Collect information concerning production and post-production; 2. Members of risk management assess if there are hazards or hazardous situations not previously identified, if the risk(s) from hazardous situations become unacceptable, whether the overall residual risk is still acceptable in relation to benefits of intended use, and whether the generally acknowledged state of the art has changed; 3. Analyze and assess risk(s) and make risk control plan and actions if necessary; 4. Track the implementation of risk control measures. Reference: Section 4.11.1 in Risk Management Control Regulation (QI-7.3-22). Output: Report of Post-market Risk Management.

Personnel qualification requirements: Chief engineer - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than three years work experience. Product manager - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than three years design experience. Project manager - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Hardware design director - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Software design director - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Mechanical design director - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Hardware design personnel - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Software design personnel - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Mechanical design personnel - Mechano-electronic related specialities, more than one year design experience. Process design personnel - Electrics or mechanics or other related engineering specialities, more than one year design experience. Quality management personnel - Electrics or mechanics or other related engineering specialities, more than one year design experience. Sales personnel - No special requirement, familiar with handling of customer complaints process. Certification personnel - Biomedicine or mechano-electronic or other related specialities, more than two years work experience. Personnel with medical background - Biology or clinical medicine or other medical related specialities, more than three years clinical experience.

Severity Classification: Catastrophic (Class S=5) - Result in patient death; Critical (Class S=4) - Result in permanent impairment or life-threatening injury; Serious (Class S=3) - Result in injury or impairment requiring professional medical intervention; Minor (Class S=2) - Result in temporary injury or impairment not requiring professional medical intervention; Negligible (Class S=1) - Inconvenience or temporary discomfort.

Semiquantitative Probability Classification: Frequent (Class P=6) - probability ≥10⁻³; Probable (Class P=5) - <10⁻³ ≥10⁻⁴; Occasional (Class P=4) - <10⁻⁴ ≥10⁻⁵; Remote (Class P=3) - <10⁻⁵ ≥10⁻⁶; Improbable (Class P=2) - <10⁻⁶ ≥10⁻⁸; Few (Class P=1) - <10⁻⁸.

Risk Acceptance Criteria: A risk matrix is used combining Severity (1-5) and Probability (1-6). Risks are classified as either 'Not acceptable' (unacceptable risk, risk control measures are required) or 'Acceptable' (insignificant/negligible risk, no risk control measures required). The manufacturer shall reduce risk as far as possible using the following risk control options in priority order: (a) eliminate or reduce risks as far as possible through safe design and manufacture; (b) where appropriate, take adequate protection measures, including alarms if necessary, in relation to risks that cannot be eliminated; (c) provide information for safety (warnings/precautions/contra-indications) and, where appropriate, training to users.

Residual Risk Acceptance Criteria for Single Residual Risk: When a risk falls in the 'Not acceptable' area, risk control measures must be taken. After taking measures, the risk becomes a residual risk. If this residual risk still falls in the 'Not acceptable' area per Section 3.3 Risk Acceptance Criteria, a risk-benefit analysis must be conducted. The residual risk will be acceptable when there are reasonable reasons to support that the benefits outweigh the risks.

The benefits related to the intended use of the medical device are weighed against the overall residual risk. Benefits can be described by their magnitude or extent, the probability of experiencing the benefit within the intended patient populations, and the duration and frequency of the benefit. The evaluation may take into account knowledge of the intended medical indication, the generally acknowledged state of the art in technology and medicine, and the availability of alternative medical devices or treatments.

Visual representations of the residual risks can be useful. Each individual residual risk can be shown in a risk matrix as shown in section 3.3. If more than 1/2 of the risks are in the higher severity regions or in the higher probability regions of the risk matrix, or clusters of risks are borderline, then the distribution of the risks can indicate that the overall residual risk might not be acceptable, even if each individual risk has been judged acceptable.

Overall risk-benefit analysis: when the benefits outweigh the overall residual risks, the overall residual risks are acceptable. If the overall residual risks are acceptable after evaluation, then the significant residual risks shall be notified to the users and involve the information in the accompanying documents. If the overall residual risks are not acceptable after evaluation, then additional risk control measures shall be taken, or the modification to the medical devices may be required.

Risk Control Measures Verification Criteria: We verify the risk control measures of the initial risks and the residual risks in accordance with the document Verification in Design and Development Control Procedure.
